preset.description: A snare built from a modal drum head and a separate noise-bank wire layer: organic and balanced.

help.text:
Two Perc Voices: a Modal head at 195 Hz with moderate damping, and a Noise Bank layer for the wires, high-passed at 2.5 kHz.

One Trig fires both. Patch a trigger there and take Out L/R. Velocity feeds the accent of both.

Tip: change the level of the Wires layer in the mixer to go from a loosely wound snare to a tight one.

preset.description: Three different claps on one trigger, spread across the stereo field: a big, thick handclap.

help.text:
Three claps in one mixer: a Ring Clap at 1 kHz on the left, a Punch Clap at 1.6 kHz in the middle and another Ring Clap at 2.2 kHz on the right, each with a different burst spacing.

One Trig fires all three. Patch a trigger there and use both Out L and Out R. Velocity reaches every layer.

Tip: it is thick and loud, so lower the centre clap's level if it sits on top of a snare.

preset.description: One crisp hand slap with no bursts: a dry, snappy click for sparse, minimal patterns.

help.text:
A Punch Clap with a single burst, a high 2.4 kHz tone and a very short decay (0.12 s), so it is one clean slap rather than a flutter.

Patch a trigger into Trig and take Out L/R. Velocity scales the hit.

Tip: raise Bursts on the clap to turn it into a classic flam.

preset.description: A handclap with a short ping-pong echo: a dubby clap that doubles itself across the stereo field.

help.text:
A Ring Clap at 1.3 kHz into a Delay at 110 ms on the left and 165 ms on the right, in ping-pong mode with low feedback and a high cut that darkens each repeat.

Patch a trigger into Trig and use both Out L and Out R. The Tone input opens the echo's high cut.

Tip: raise the Delay feedback for more repeats, but the clap will then run into the next beat.

preset.description: A metallic, wavefolded snare from the Macro Osc: a clanging, hard-edged industrial hit.

help.text:
A Macro Osc in its Snare model pushed into a Folder, then a high-pass at 150 Hz. The folding adds a bright, inharmonic edge to the noise.

Patch a trigger into Trig and take Out L/R. Velocity feeds the oscillator's accent. The Tone input opens a low-pass on the result.

Tip: increase the Folder's Fold for a more ringing, metallic snare.

preset.description: Very bright, thin hats with an airy sparkle: closed ticks and a short, shimmering open hat.

help.text:
A Punch Hats module tuned up four semitones with a bright Tone and a high-pass at 8 kHz, so only the sparkle is left. A small, short Reverb adds air. Closed cuts the open hat.

Patch triggers into Closed and Open and take Out L/R. The Tone input moves the high-pass.

Tip: keep the open hat short (the Open Decay) in busy patterns, since the reverb adds to its tail.

preset.description: Hats from an old, worn record: crushed, low-passed and a little loose, for boom-bap and lo-fi.

help.text:
A Ring Hats module into a Crunch with 9 bits and some sample-rate reduction, then a low-pass at 7 kHz to take the digital edge off. Closed cuts the open hat.

Patch triggers into Closed and Open and take Out L/R. The Tone input opens the low-pass.

Tip: lower Bits on the Crunch for a more worn-out sound.

preset.description: Two hat modules stacked: a metallic ring layer for body and a crunchy punch layer for sizzle.

help.text:
A Ring Hats layer (6 dB down) and a Punch Hats layer with Crunch, both listening to Closed and Open. A high-pass at 4 kHz keeps the low end clean. Each module cuts its own open hat on Closed.

Patch triggers into Closed and Open and take Out L/R. Velocity reaches both layers.

Tip: use the mixer levels to move between a darker metallic hat and a crisper, brighter one.

preset.description: Dark, short, woody hats like a hi-hat pedal chick: a soft, low tick instead of a bright sizzle.

help.text:
A Ring Hats module with very short decays and a low Tone, band-passed around 3 kHz so it has a dry, papery chick rather than a long hiss. Closed cuts the open hat.

Patch triggers into Closed and Open and take Out L/R. The Tone input moves the band-pass.

Tip: play it on beats 2 and 4 for a classic swing feel.

preset.description: A shaker instead of a hat: a quick grain of noise for Closed and a longer swish for Open.

help.text:
Two Perc Voices in the Noise Bank engine: a very short one for Closed and a longer one with a gradual feel for Open, both high-passed at 3 kHz. A Closed trigger chokes the open swish.

Patch triggers into Closed and Open and take Out L/R. Velocity feeds both voices.

Tip: alternate Closed and Open on 16ths for a shaker groove; a raised Pitch makes it sound finer.

preset.description: A low, dry ride with a muted ping: a jazz ride that sits quietly behind other instruments.

help.text:
A Punch Cymbal in its Ride voice tuned down five semitones with low Tone and little crunch, then a low-pass at 6 kHz so the shimmer stays soft.

Patch a trigger into Trig and take Out L/R. The Tone input opens the low-pass.

Tip: play steady 8ths with changing Velocity; the quiet hits keep it from standing out.

preset.description: A deep, long gong-like crash: a low metallic clang that blooms into a slow wash.

help.text:
A Ring Cymbal tuned an octave down with a 5 s decay, over a Perc Voice in its Modal engine for the low clang, into a Reverb with a long tail.

Patch a trigger into Trig and take Out L/R. Velocity scales both layers.

Tip: use it for transitions and drops. Its tail is long, so give it a bar of space.

preset.description: A broken, saturated crash: a noisy, distorted cymbal for aggressive music.

help.text:
A Punch Cymbal in its Crash voice with Crunch at maximum, into a Crunch module with drive and 8 bits, then a high-pass at 500 Hz.

Patch a trigger into Trig and take Out L/R. Velocity sets the level.

Tip: it is harsh and bright, so it works best as an accent rather than a constant ride.

preset.description: A short crash cut off almost at once: a quick, splashy accent that never rings on.

help.text:
A Ring Cymbal with a short 0.45 s decay and a high Tone, shaped with a Compressor that clamps the tail, like a crash grabbed by the hand.

Patch a trigger into Trig and take Out L/R. Velocity scales the hit.

Tip: use it before a pause for an accent that stops dead.

preset.description: A clear, bell-like ping: a short, pitched ride bell for accents and cowbell-style parts.

help.text:
A Perc Voice in its FM engine at 1.2 kHz with a short, damped decay for the ping, plus a Punch Cymbal Ride layer, quietly, for the sizzle behind it. A high-pass at 400 Hz keeps it clean.

Patch a trigger into Trig and take Out L/R. Velocity feeds both layers.

Tip: change the voice's Morph to move from a clean bell to a harsher, clangier one.

preset.description: A tight rack tom with a big pitch dive and a hint of room; retune it for a whole kit of toms.

help.text:
A Punch Tom at 180 Hz with a strong bend and a medium decay, into a small, quiet Reverb.

Patch a trigger into Trig and take Out L/R. Velocity scales the hit.

Tip: copy the cell three times and set Tune of the Punch Tom to 180, 130 and 95 for a descending fill.

preset.description: A hollow, woody log drum with a soft attack, good for tuned percussion lines.

help.text:
A Perc Voice in its Modal engine at 160 Hz. Low Tone keeps the partials close to a hollow wooden tube, and Damp ends the ring quickly.

Patch a trigger into Trig and Out L/R. Velocity feeds the voice's accent.

Tip: patch a sequencer's pitch into the voice's Pitch for a bubbling marimba-like bass line.

preset.description: A bright, short bongo with a dry slap on the skin.

help.text:
A Perc Voice in its Modal engine at 480 Hz with a strong Click for the slap and a short decay.

Patch a trigger into Trig and take Out L/R. Velocity feeds the accent.

Tip: pair it with a copy tuned down a fourth (Pitch 360) and play the two in alternation.

preset.description: A ringing timbale: a tight shell tone with a rim crack on top.

help.text:
Two layers: a Ring Tom tuned high with little bend and a short decay for the shell, and a Punch Rim for the crack.

One Trig fires both. Patch a trigger there and take Out L/R. Velocity reaches both.

Tip: lower the rim's gain for a softer hit, and play fast fills on the off-beats.

preset.description: A high woodblock tick with a touch of body.

help.text:
A Ring Rim on its Clave voice, tuned up seven semitones, plus a very short Modal Perc Voice tone underneath for body.

Patch a trigger into Trig and Out L/R. Velocity reaches both layers.

Tip: use it as a hi-fi metronome click or for dry 8th-note ostinatos.

preset.description: Two metal bells in one hit, a high and a low, panned apart.

help.text:
Two Ring Cowbell layers, one tuned up seven semitones and panned right, the other tuned down two and panned left, both with a short decay.

Patch a trigger into Trig and take Out L/R. Velocity scales both.

Tip: set the two Tune knobs to a different interval for another character, a fourth is classic.

preset.description: A scratchy, band-passed noise burst like beads on a metal drum.

help.text:
A Perc Voice in the Noise Bank engine at 4 kHz with a very short decay, through a band-pass around 5 kHz that removes the hiss above and the thump below.

Patch a trigger into Trig and Out L/R. Velocity feeds the accent.

Tip: shift the band-pass Cutoff up for a smaller, brighter shaker.

preset.description: A goblet drum slap: sharp edge, open skin and a short wooden resonance.

help.text:
A Perc Voice in its Modal engine at 260 Hz with a high Click and a gentle sweep, plus a short noise burst high-passed for the slap of the hand.

Patch a trigger into Trig and take Out L/R. Velocity feeds both layers.

Tip: lower the Pitch of the first layer for a bass tone.

preset.description: A huge, slow ceremonial drum with a long boom and a stadium tail.

help.text:
A Ring Tom at 62 Hz with a one-and-a-half second decay and a lot of noise, into a Hall reverb.

Patch a trigger into Trig and Out L/R. Velocity sets the level of the strike.

Tip: play it on the first beat of a section in a slow tempo and let the reverb fill the gap.

preset.description: A tiny, high, long-ringing metal triangle.

help.text:
A Perc Voice in its Modal engine at 3.2 kHz with the Tone knob at maximum and a long, lightly damped decay, high-passed to keep it thin.

Patch a trigger into Trig and take Out L/R. Velocity feeds the accent.

Tip: use a shorter Decay and play it on the off-beat for a dry disco ting.

preset.description: A pure, slowly fading ping that echoes away like a signal under water.

help.text:
A Perc Voice in its FM engine at 1.4 kHz with almost no sweep and a half-second decay, into a Delay in ping-pong mode with a dark feedback.

Patch a trigger into Trig and Out L/R. Velocity feeds the accent.

Tip: set the delay's Sync to Tempo to make the echoes fall on the beat.

preset.description: Two bright square-ish chirps one fifth apart: a game pickup sound.

help.text:
Two Perc Voice layers in the FM engine, 1.2 kHz and 1.8 kHz, both short, mixed together and crunched slightly for an 8-bit edge.

Patch a trigger into Trig and take Out L/R. Velocity sets the level.

Tip: lower Bits in the Crunch for more lo-fi grit.

preset.description: A burst of bright dust and a ringing glassy shard, high and sparkling.

help.text:
A Macro Osc in its Dust model for the falling shards and a high Modal Voice for the ring, summed and high-passed, into a small bright Reverb.

One Trig fires both. Patch a trigger there and take Out L/R. Velocity reaches both.

Tip: raise the high-pass Cutoff for thinner glass.

preset.description: A rubbery spring wobble: a falling FM tone swept through a phaser.

help.text:
A Perc Voice in its FM engine at 500 Hz with a long, deep downward sweep and a low Tone, through a slow Phaser with feedback for the wobble.

Patch a trigger into Trig and Out L/R. Velocity feeds the accent.

Tip: raise the Phaser's Rate for a faster spring.

preset.description: A hissing gust of high noise that swells down into a soft tail.

help.text:
A Perc Voice in its Noise Bank engine at 4 kHz with a long one-second decay, high-passed and widened by a short Reverb.

Patch a trigger into Trig and take Out L/R. Velocity scales the burst.

Tip: use it on the offbeat as a breathing hat replacement, or hold it back for builds.

preset.description: A dry crackling burst like a bad cable, shaped by a band-pass and a little grit.

help.text:
A Macro Osc in its Dust model with a quarter-second decay through a band-pass around 4 kHz and a Crunch for grit.

Patch a trigger into Trig and Out L/R. Velocity feeds the oscillator's accent.

Tip: fire it in short rolls to make a stuttering glitch.

preset.description: A short, throaty vowel hit: a robotic 'oh' that decays quickly.

help.text:
A Macro Osc in its Vowel model, with Tone moving the vowel and a short decay, into a bit of Crunch.

Patch a trigger into Trig and take Out L/R. Velocity feeds the accent.

Tip: change the Macro Osc's Tone to sweep through other vowels.

preset.description: A deep, bowed-metal gong swelling slowly in a huge space.

help.text:
A Perc Voice in its Modal engine at 120 Hz with Tone at maximum so the partials turn metallic, a long decay and an added dull click, into a big Reverb.

Patch a trigger into Trig and Out L/R. Velocity scales the strike.

Tip: use it for a slow downbeat; raise the reverb Decay for an even longer wash.

preset.description: A tuned glass chime with an octave-up shimmer trailing behind it.

help.text:
A Modal Voice struck two octaves up, fed through a Pitch Shifter a fifth up with some feedback, into a Reverb.

Patch a trigger into Trig and take Out L/R. Velocity sets the strike strength.

Tip: change the shifter's Pitch to 12 for a pure octave shimmer.

preset.description: A metal clang pulled out of tune by a frequency shifter: inharmonic and unsettling.

help.text:
A Ring Cowbell with a long decay through a Freq Shifter with feedback, which makes the partials drift apart into a spiralling, bell-like ring.

Patch a trigger into Trig and Out L/R. Velocity scales it.

Tip: set the shifter's Shift to a negative value for a downward spiral.

preset.description: A twelve-step triplet bass figure in E minor that gallops root, root, octave: play a short, punchy bass Voice Cell for driving metal and electro-rock lines. Shared inputs Transpose and Reset.

help.text:
A Step Sequencer with twelve steps on triplet eighths in E natural minor, three octaves down from the middle. Every beat is a gallop: root, root, octave, and the last beat climbs through the fifth and the seventh. The first note of each group is accented, the others ride lower.

Patch Notes into a Voice Cell set to one voice with a short decay; Pitch and Gate are there if you would rather drive your own oscillator and envelope. A pitch into Transpose changes the key, a trigger into Reset restarts the figure. It follows the transport unless you patch Clock.

Tip: distortion after a sawtooth bass makes it sound like a charging bass guitar.

preset.description: Eight C major pentatonic notes played up and back again in eighths, with a Variation input that nudges random steps by an octave: a bright climbing figure for a pluck or a bell voice.

help.text:
A Step Sequencer with eight steps in C major pentatonic, running in Ping-Pong direction: up the scale and back down without repeating the end notes. The Variation knob lets random steps jump by up to an octave and a half; at zero the figure is exactly the same every time.

Patch Notes into a Voice Cell with a pluck, bell or mallet sound. The Variation input is added to the Variation knob, so a slow LFO or a dial brings the figure to life, and a pitch into Transpose moves the key. It follows the transport unless you patch Clock.

Tip: raise Variation only during the last bar of a phrase for a spontaneous fill.

preset.description: Short syncopated A Dorian chord stabs: a Step Sequencer fires root notes that a Chord Quantizer turns into smooth-voiced seventh chords. Play a keys or organ Voice Cell. Shared inputs Transpose and Strum.

help.text:
A Step Sequencer places root notes on the off-beats of a bar in A Dorian. A Chord Quantizer in Diatonic mode turns every root into a four-note seventh chord from the same scale, voiced Drop 2 with voice leading so neighbouring chords move as little as possible.

Patch Notes into a polyphonic Voice Cell (electric piano, organ or a short synth chord) and keep the release short. Root carries the chord root as a pitch for a bass voice. The Strum input is added to the Strum time, spreading each chord into a quick roll, and a pitch into Transpose changes the key. It follows the transport unless you patch Clock.

Tip: play the Root output on a bass voice an octave down to get the whole rhythm section.

preset.description: Hold a chord on a keyboard and it plays the notes from the outside in over three octaves, with latch on so you can let go: patch a Keyboard or the host's MIDI into Notes and the output into any Voice Cell.

help.text:
An Arpeggiator in Converge pattern over three octaves on sixteenth notes, with swing and Latch on: it alternates between the lowest and the highest held note and moves toward the middle, so a chord folds in on itself. With Latch on, it keeps playing after you release the keys until you play a new chord.

Patch a Keyboard (or the host's MIDI notes) into the Notes input, and the Notes output into a Voice Cell. Pitch and Gate are there too. A trigger into Reset restarts the pattern. It follows the transport unless you patch Clock.

Tip: play a four-note chord and change it every bar for a pulsing, ever-shifting texture.

preset.description: A four-lane drum pattern with ratcheted hats, ghost notes and a fill that appears while its input is held: patch Notes into a drum machine's MIDI input or each Gate into a drum voice. Shared inputs Fill and Hat Mute.

help.text:
A Gate Sequencer with four lanes at sixteenth notes: kick, snare, closed hat and an open-hat lane that is twelve steps long and so drifts against the other three. The hats ratchet in places, the snare has a ghost note and the kick has coin-flip hits. While Fill is held, extra snare hits appear and some kicks drop out.

Notes carries all four lanes as General MIDI drum notes (kick, snare, closed and open hat): patch it into a drum machine cell's Notes input. Or use the Kick, Snare, Hat and Open gates on single drum voices. A gate into Fill adds the fill, a gate into Hat Mute silences the hats. It follows the transport unless you patch Clock.

Tip: hold Fill on the last bar of every four for a turnaround.

preset.description: No clock at all: two slow LFOs steer a crosshair over an 8 × 8 grid of D Dorian phrases and a note sounds whenever it enters a new cell. Shared inputs X and Y push the crosshair by hand; Mod rises with the row.

help.text:
A Cartesian Seq in Cartesian mode: X and Y choose the column and the row directly, and with Sample set to Change a note plays as soon as the crosshair moves into a different cell. Two slow triangle LFOs steer the crosshair so it drifts across all 64 cells in D Dorian, low rows to high rows.

Patch Notes into a Voice Cell with a soft, long-release sound. The X and Y inputs are added to the LFO movement: patch an XY Pad or two Dials and you steer the walk yourself. Mod carries the value stored in each cell, which is higher in the upper rows; patch it into a filter cutoff. The walk is independent of the transport and keeps going when it stops.

Tip: make the voice's release long enough that the notes overlap into a slow, pealing melody.

preset.description: A Stage Seq random-walks one step at a time through eight stages in D Phrygian Dominant, so the riff meanders but never leaps: a winding, eastern-sounding line for a reedy or plucked voice. Shared inputs Transpose and Hold.

help.text:
A Stage Sequencer with eight stages in D Phrygian Dominant. Mode Brownian moves to a neighbouring stage at random each step, never farther, so the line wanders up and down the scale like a snake. Stages differ in length (1 to 4 pulses), gate mode (hold, repeat, ratchet) and slide, so a given walk sounds varied.

Patch Notes into a Voice Cell; with Legato mode and some Glide the slides curve between notes. Pitch and Gate are available as well. A pitch into Transpose changes the key; a gate into Hold makes the current stage repeat. It follows the transport unless you patch Clock.

Tip: change the Seed setting for a different walk with the same notes.

preset.description: A Rhythm Bank rhythm decides when to play and a random value, snapped to F Lydian, decides what: a melody over an even, spread-out rhythm that never repeats its notes the same way. Shared inputs Pattern and Transpose.

help.text:
A Rhythm Bank in the Even family (evenly spread hits over sixteen steps) gives the gate. On every hit a Random module picks a new value, a Quantizer snaps it to F Lydian over a range of one and a half octaves, and CV to Notes combines pitch and gate into notes.

Patch Notes into a Voice Cell. Pitch, Gate and Cycle (a trigger at each pass through the rhythm) are also available. The Pattern input is added to the Pattern knob: a slow LFO or a dial moves through the library of rhythms, and a pitch into Transpose shifts the key. It follows the transport unless you patch Clock.

Tip: set Loop on the Random module higher for repeating phrases, or lower for endless variation.

preset.description: A Shift Register mutates a melody in A minor pentatonic; bit 1 plays a lead and bit 5 plays a bass two octaves down, so the bass echoes the lead's pattern four steps later. Two Notes outputs: Lead and Bass. Shared inputs Lock and Transpose.

help.text:
An 8-bit Shift Register clocked on eighth notes in A minor pentatonic. Its first bit plays the lead through CV to Notes. Its fifth bit plays a bass: each time it fires, a Quantizer Suite samples the register's pitch two octaves lower. Bit 5 is the first bit's pattern delayed by four steps, so the bass is a canon of the melody.

Patch Lead into a Voice Cell for the melody and Bass into another voice for the bass. Lock is added to the Lock knob: up freezes the loop, down mutates it. A pitch into Transpose changes the key. It follows the transport unless you patch Clock.

Tip: freeze the loop with Lock, then listen: the bass always plays what the lead played four steps ago.

preset.description: A map of kick, snare and hat rhythms you travel with X and Y, with General MIDI drum notes out (and a trigger per drum): patch Notes into a drum machine and ride the map with an XY Pad. Shared inputs X, Y and Fill.

help.text:
A Drum Map holds a map of kick, snare and hat patterns; X and Y pick where you stand on the map and the rhythm morphs as you move. The three densities are set to a medium level, the chaos to a slow, gentle drift every four bars, and the accent and swing are tuned for a laid-back groove.

Notes carries the three drums as General MIDI drum notes: patch it into a drum machine cell's Notes input. Kick, Snare and Hats are triggers for single drum voices. The X and Y inputs are added to the knobs, so an XY Pad gives you live control; a gate into Fill adds extra hits for a fill. It follows the transport unless you patch Clock.

Tip: move X and Y slowly across the pad between sections, and hold Fill before each change.

preset.description: A dense, bright plate reverb with a short pre-delay and a two-second tail: vocals, snares and keys gain a polished sheen. Shared inputs Mix and Decay.

help.text:
A single Reverb with high diffusion, little damping and a tone tilted bright. Pre-delay is 12 ms so the attack of the sound stays clear before the plate blooms. The reverb is 30 percent wet.

Patch a sound into In L/R and take Out L/R onwards. Mix is added to the reverb's Mix knob and Decay to its Decay knob, which stretches the tail from a tight plate towards a hall.

Tip: put it on a snare and pull Decay down for a classic gated-feeling splash.

preset.description: A single dark 110 ms slapback with a whisper of feedback, smeared by a short room: it thickens guitars and vocals without becoming an echo. Shared inputs Mix and Time.

help.text:
A Delay at 110 ms on the left and 135 ms on the right, with very little feedback, a high cut at 3.5 kHz so the repeat sits behind the sound, and a small Room reverb after it.

Patch a sound into In L/R and take Out L/R onwards. Mix is added to the delay's Mix and Time to both delay times, so you can slide between a doubling and a clear slap.

Tip: use it on a dry guitar or a vocal, and turn Mix down until you only notice it when it is gone.

preset.description: Tempo-synced echoes that bounce between the ears: eighth-triplets on the left, dotted eighths on the right, each repeat a little darker. Shared inputs Feedback and Mix.

help.text:
A Delay in tempo-sync mode and Ping-Pong mode, with 1/8T on the left and 1/8. on the right. Low and high cut shape every repeat, so the echoes thin out as they fade. The delay follows the transport tempo.

Patch a sound into In L/R and take Out L/R onwards. Feedback is added to the delay's Feedback and Mix to its Mix.

Tip: it is made for sparse plucks and short hits; with a busy part, keep Mix low.

preset.description: Six delay lines fed back into each other in a mesh, with scattered and jittered times and some reversed taps: a cloud of echoes that never repeats itself the same way. Shared inputs Feedback and Scatter.

help.text:
A Delay Net with six taps in Mesh routing. Scatter spreads the tap times, Jitter makes them wander, a share of the taps play backwards, and every feedback pass picks up a little character and darkness.

Patch a sound into In L/R and take Out L/R onwards. Feedback is added to the feedback knob (above about 90 percent it sustains for a long time) and Scatter to the scatter knob.

Tip: feed it short notes and sweep Scatter slowly while the cloud rings.

preset.description: Two choruses at unrelated slow speeds, one with a longer delay, blended and widened: strings, pads and electric pianos melt into a big ensemble. Shared inputs Depth and Mix.

help.text:
Two Chorus modules in a row. The first is quick and shallow with a short delay, the second is slow and deep with a longer delay, and both spread their voices wide. Together they smear the pitch in two different time scales, like a string ensemble.

Patch a sound into In L/R and take Out L/R onwards. Depth is added to the depth of both choruses; Mix to the mix of the second one.

Tip: it is made for chords and sustained sounds; single notes get a seasick detune.

preset.description: Twelve allpass stages with negative feedback, swept wide and slowly: a hollow, glassy phaser that rolls through guitars, synth pads and drum loops. Shared inputs Speed and Centre.

help.text:
A Phaser with twelve stages, negative feedback, a wide sweep and the right ear offset from the left. Negative feedback gives the hollow, glassy colour instead of the nasal sound of positive feedback.

Patch a sound into In L/R and take Out L/R onwards. Speed is added to the Rate knob and Centre moves the middle of the sweep up or down. It does not follow the transport.

Tip: raise Centre for a brighter, airier sweep on pads; lower it for a heavy, dark roll on bass-rich loops.

preset.description: The reverb's tail is sent up an octave and back into the reverb so every echo climbs: a bright, celestial halo above pads and single notes. Shared inputs Mix, Climb and Freeze.

help.text:
A Reverb whose wet signal goes through a Pitch Shifter (up twelve semitones), a VCA named Climb and a Limiter, and back into the reverb. Each echo is an octave higher than the last, and the limiter keeps the loop from running away.

Patch a sound into In L/R and take Out L/R onwards. Mix is added to the reverb mix, Climb to the loop gain (more means more ascending echoes) and a gate into Freeze holds the tail. The tail is long, about twenty seconds.

Tip: play sustained chords, then raise Climb slowly for a rising wall.

preset.description: A slow sine swells the left channel while it fades the right, and the other way round: the whole image sways between the ears. Shared inputs Rate and Depth.

help.text:
An LFO feeds a Multiplier named Depth. One output drives a VCA on the left channel, the other, inverted, drives a VCA on the right, so the loudness of the two sides moves in opposite directions.

Patch a sound into In L/R and take Out L/R onwards. Rate is added to the LFO rate and Depth is added to the Multiplier, so zero depth leaves the sound still and centred. It does not follow the transport.

Tip: a stereo source works best; with a mono source, the pan is more obvious than with a wide one.

preset.description: A gate holds whatever the grains have just heard and spreads it into a slowly drifting, endless cloud under a deep reverb. Shared inputs Freeze, Mix and Drift.

help.text:
Grains records the input into a buffer and plays it back as a soft cloud with generous blur. A Reverb follows with a long decay. When Freeze is high, the buffer stops recording and the cloud keeps playing what it holds.

Patch a sound into In L/R and take Out L/R onwards. A gate into Freeze holds the moment; Mix is added to the Grains mix and Drift to its Texture knob, which changes how scattered the cloud is. The tail is long.

Tip: play a chord, hold Freeze, then play something new over the drone.

preset.description: A frequency shifter whose echoes feed back through a delay, so each pass lifts the spectrum a little: inharmonic bell spirals that climb out of any note. Shared inputs Shift and Feedback.

help.text:
A Frequency Shifter moves the whole spectrum up by a fixed number of hertz, not by a musical interval, and feeds it back through a short delay. Every pass shifts again, so a plucked note turns into a spiral of inharmonic partials. Spread makes the two ears go in opposite directions.

Patch a sound into In L/R and take Out L/R onwards. Shift is added to the shifter's Shift knob and Feedback to its Feedback knob. The tail rings for a while.

Tip: use single plucks or drum hits, and keep Feedback below the point where it starts to sing on its own.

preset.description: Tremolo with two LFOs, one per side, set a quarter cycle apart so the level seesaws across the stereo field. Shared inputs Rate, Depth, Spread and Shape.

help.text:
Two LFOs scale the left and right signals through a Multiplier. The second LFO starts 90 degrees behind the first, so the level of one side is rising while the other falls: Spread widens or closes that offset, down to a plain mono tremolo.

Patch a sound into In L/R and take Out L/R onwards. Rate, Depth, Spread and Shape are added to the LFO rate, the depth knob of the Multiplier, the phase offset and the LFO wave (sine, triangle, saw, square, random). To lock the speed to the tempo, open the cell and set both LFOs' Sync to a note value.

Tip: set Shape to square, Depth to the top and Spread to 180 degrees for a hard left-right chop.

preset.description: A rotating-speaker effect: a crossover feeds a fast horn and a slower drum, each swung by Doppler delay and amplitude swell, with a Slow/Fast switch that spins up and down over a couple of seconds. Shared inputs Mix, Fast, Speed, Depth, Mics and Split.

help.text:
A low-pass and a high-pass filter split the sound at 800 Hz. Each band goes through a modulated delay, so the pitch leans up and down as the imaginary speaker swings past, and through a level swell from the other two outputs of the same quad LFO. The horn (highs) turns faster than the drum (lows). The two stereo channels listen from opposite sides of the turn.

Patch a sound into In L/R and take Out L/R onwards. The Fast button inside the cell, or a gate into Fast, switches between slow and fast; a slew ramps the speed over about 1.8 seconds so it accelerates and coasts like a real rotor. Speed adds to both rotor rates, Depth to the Doppler swing, Mics to the quarter-cycle offset between the four LFO phases, Split to the crossover frequency and Mix to the dry/wet balance.

Tip: put it after an organ or an electric piano and hit Fast on the chorus of the song.

preset.description: Splits the stereo image into its centre and its sides, gives each its own filter, saturation and level, then puts it back together. Shared inputs Mid, Side, Mid Drive, Side Drive, Bass Mono and Mid Tone.

help.text:
A Matrix Mixer encodes left and right into Mid (what they share) and Side (what differs). The Mid goes through a low-pass filter, a Saturator and a VCA; the Side through a high-pass filter, a Saturator and a VCA; a second Matrix Mixer decodes them back to left and right. With everything at its default the sound comes out nearly unchanged but a little wider.

Patch a sound into In L/R and take Out L/R onwards. Mid and Side are added to the two levels (Side above one widens, at zero the result is mono), Mid Drive and Side Drive to the saturation, Bass Mono to the Side's high-pass frequency, which keeps low notes in the middle, and Mid Tone to the Mid's low-pass.

Tip: drive only the Side a little and pull Bass Mono up to 200 Hz for a wide, gritty sound with a solid centre.

preset.description: An equal-power auto-pan with a twist: the louder the signal, the further it is pushed to one side. Shared inputs Pan, Rate, Depth, Push and Shape.

help.text:
An LFO sweeps the pan of a mixer channel; an Envelope Follower adds a second push that follows the loudness, so loud notes swing out to the right while quiet tails settle in the middle. The mixer's pan is equal-power, so the level stays steady as it moves.

Patch a sound into In L/R and take Out L/R onwards. Pan is added to the centre position, Rate to the sweep speed, Depth to the sweep width (zero stops the sweep), Push to the loudness amount and Shape to the LFO wave.

Tip: set Depth to zero and use only Push on a drum loop: each hit leans right and falls back with the release.

preset.description: Reshapes the attack and the sustain of any sound by comparing a fast and a slow loudness follower. Shared inputs Attack, Sustain, Sense and Grit.

help.text:
Two Envelope Followers listen to the input, one quick and one slow. Their difference is positive at the start of a sound (the quick one is ahead) and negative while it dies away. The positive part, scaled by Attack, and the negative part, scaled by Sustain, are added to a gain of one and drive a VCA. A little Saturator after it adds grit.

Patch a sound into In L/R and take Out L/R onwards. Attack is added to the transient amount (more snap), Sustain to the tail amount (more body, or less when the knob inside is negative), Sense to the follower sensitivity and Grit to the drive of the final saturation.

Tip: for tighter drums leave Attack up and set the Sustain scale inside the cell below zero.

preset.description: A spectral delay: the sound is cut into five bands and each band gets its own echo time, so lows answer first and highs trail behind, spread across the stereo field. Shared inputs Time, Stretch, Feedback, Tilt and Mix.

help.text:
A Filter Bank splits the input into ten bands; two Matrix Mixers gather them into five groups of two. Each group goes through its own Delay, from 70 ms for the lows to 480 ms for the highs, and a third Matrix Mixer spreads the five echoes from left to right across the stereo field. The dry sound comes back on a Crossfader.

Patch a sound into In L/R and take Out L/R onwards. Time is added to all five delay times, Stretch to each time in growing steps (the higher the band, the more it moves), Feedback to the repeats, Tilt to the bank's tilt, which fades low bands against high ones, and Mix to the dry/wet balance.

Tip: a short plucked sound with Stretch up turns into a rising or falling shimmer.

preset.description: A big reverb that is only let through while the dry sound is loud, then cut off with an adjustable hold, and that rings longer after harder hits. Shared inputs Mix, Hold, Threshold and Decay.

help.text:
The Verb is fully wet. An Envelope Follower listens to the dry input; its gate output, smoothed by a slew, opens a VCA after the reverb, so the tail is chopped when the sound stops. The follower's level also lengthens the reverb Decay a little, so hard hits bloom bigger than soft ones.

Patch a sound into In L/R and take Out L/R onwards. Hold is added to the slew time (how long the tail lingers before closing), Threshold to the loudness needed to open the gate, Decay to the reverb time and Mix to the dry/wet balance.

Tip: a snare with Hold at a quarter turn gives a short, explosive room; with Hold up it turns into a swell.

preset.description: A tempo-synced ping-pong echo that gets out of the way while you play and swells back in the gaps. Shared inputs Duck, Recover, Feedback and Level.

help.text:
A fully wet Delay (dotted eighth on the left, quarter on the right, ping-pong) goes through a VCA. An Envelope Follower on the dry signal lowers that VCA by the amount of the Duck scale, so the echoes sit back under loud playing and rise again over the Recover time. The dry sound always passes untouched.

Patch a sound into In L/R and take Out L/R onwards. The delay follows the transport tempo or a cable into Clock. Duck is added to the ducking depth, Recover to the follower release, Feedback to the repeats and Level to the loudness of the echoes.

Tip: with Duck at the top, a sustained pad stays clean and the echoes only show up in the rests.

preset.description: Slows everything down to a halt, darkening as it goes, and spins back up on release; a hand button or a gate triggers it, and a wobble grows as the speed falls. Shared inputs Stop, Time and Wobble.

help.text:
A fully wet Delay is normally set to one millisecond, so the sound passes through unchanged. When the Stop button (inside the cell) or the Stop gate is held, an envelope pushes the delay time up, which makes the sound play slower and lower until it almost stops; at the same time the delay's high cut closes. A slow LFO scaled by the same envelope adds wow as the speed falls. On release the envelope drops quickly and the pitch jumps back up.

Patch a sound into In L/R and take Out L/R onwards. Stop is a gate, for example from a sequencer's gate track, Time is added to the length of the slowdown and Wobble to the amount of wow.

Tip: trigger it for a bar before a drop; with Time down it becomes a quick turntable-style stop.

preset.description: Splits the sound into low, mid and high, compresses each band on its own, and puts them back; one Squeeze input pushes all three harder at once. Shared inputs Squeeze, Low Split, High Split and Parallel.

help.text:
Two crossovers (at 180 Hz and 2.5 kHz) divide the signal into three bands. Each band has its own Compressor: slow and heavy on the lows, medium on the mids, quick on the highs. An Audio Mixer sums them with its limiter on.

Patch a sound into In L/R and take Out L/R onwards. Squeeze lowers all three thresholds and raises their make-up gain together, Low Split and High Split are added to the two crossover frequencies, and Parallel is subtracted from the compressors' Mix so the untouched sound blends back in.

Tip: for a mix bus keep Squeeze low; for a drum loop push it and set Parallel to about half.

preset.description: A stereo crossover with an output per band: low, mid and high each leave on their own jacks, and the recombined sound leaves on Out L/R. Shared inputs Low Split, High Split and Mid Dip.

help.text:
Two crossovers (at 200 Hz and 3 kHz) divide the stereo input into low, mid and high. Each band is available on its own pair of jacks (Low L/R, Mid L/R, High L/R) to be processed separately, for example with a different effect on every band. The Out L/R jacks hold the three bands summed again, with a dip for the mid.

Patch a sound into In L/R, take the band outputs wherever you like and bring them together again later. Low Split and High Split are added to the two crossover frequencies; Mid Dip lowers the mid band in the summed output only.

Tip: put a saturator on the lows and a delay on the highs, and mix them back on a separate mixer.

preset.description: Adds sheen on top: the highs are cut out, saturated, widened with a slow chorus and blended back in. Shared inputs Air, Freq, Drive and Width.

help.text:
A high-pass filter takes only the top of the sound, a Saturator creates new harmonics from it, a Chorus spreads those across the stereo field and a VCA sets how much of it is added to the untouched input.

Patch a sound into In L/R and take Out L/R onwards. Air is added to the amount of exciter blended in, Freq to the high-pass frequency (higher is airier and thinner), Drive to the saturation and Width to the chorus mix.

Tip: it works best on dull recordings; if the result gets hissy, lower Freq's range or turn Drive down rather than Air.

preset.description: One equaliser band whose gain rides the loudness: it can bloom or dip as you play, and it can listen to a second signal instead. Shared inputs Range, Freq, Speed and Key.

help.text:
An Envelope Follower reads the loudness of the input (and of the Key input if you patch one); a Utility scales it by the Range amount and adds it to the gain of a bell band of the EQ at 3 kHz. With a positive scale the band swells with louder playing, with a negative scale it dips, which is a de-esser or a duck for one part of the spectrum.

Patch a sound into In L/R and take Out L/R onwards. Range is added to the scale (below zero it turns the effect around), Freq to the band frequency, Speed to the follower release, and Key is an extra audio input the band also listens to.

Tip: feed a kick into Key and put the band at 80 Hz on a bass: the bass opens up on every kick.

preset.description: The dry sound with two sub copies, one and two octaves down, each darkened and drifting a little. Shared inputs Sub 1, Sub 2, Tone and Detune.

help.text:
Two Pitch Shifters move the input down 12 and 24 semitones. Each goes through a low-pass filter so the copies stay round, and an Audio Mixer blends them under the dry signal.

Patch a sound into In L/R and take Out L/R onwards. Sub 1 and Sub 2 are added to the two copies' levels, Tone to both low-pass frequencies and Detune to the fine tuning of both, one up and one down, which gives a slow beat between them.

Tip: it works best on single lines such as a bass or a lead; chords make the lowest copies muddy.

preset.description: Layers the input with three pitch-shifted copies that follow the chord of the board's Harmony Master, gliding when the chord changes. Shared inputs Stack, Glide and Spread.

help.text:
A Harmony Master supplies the board's chord. Three Math rows subtract its root from three chord tones, which gives the intervals above the root; a Utility slew per interval smooths them, and each result sets the pitch of a Pitch Shifter. An Audio Mixer puts the dry sound and the three copies together, with the copies panned apart.

Patch a sound into In L/R and take Out L/R onwards. Stack is added to the levels of the three copies, Glide to the time they slide to a new chord, and Spread to how far the copies sit left and right. Change the chord with a Harmony Master elsewhere on the board.

Tip: it is clearest on a single sustained note; change the chord with a progression and listen to the layers glide.

preset.description: Makes any sound feel like a worn record: it is band-limited, crushed, wobbled, and dusted with random pops that appear only while the music plays. Shared inputs Wear, Dust, Crackle and Warp.

help.text:
An EQ cuts the lows and the highs and adds a mid bump, a Crunch bit-crushes and lowers the sample rate, and a slow Chorus adds wow. Next to that, a Pulse Generator runs at irregular intervals, each pulse is multiplied by white noise so every pop has its own size and sign, and a second Crunch roughens it. An Envelope Follower on the input opens a VCA for the crackle, so the dust only shows up while there is sound, and fades with the tail.

Patch a sound into In L/R and take Out L/R onwards. Wear is added to the sample-rate reduction, Dust to how often the pops come, Crackle to their level and Warp to the depth of the wow.

Tip: for a scratchy intro raise Dust and Crackle together and keep Wear low.

preset.description: An echo that gets darker, dirtier and wobblier with every repeat, because the saturation, the low-pass filter and a drifting delay time all sit inside its feedback loop. Shared inputs Time, Feedback, Dark, Age and Mix.

help.text:
The dry sound and the feedback return meet in a mixer and go into a Delay. What comes out passes a Saturator and a low-pass filter, then a VCA that sets the feedback and returns to the mixer, so each repeat is warmer and duller than the one before. A slow LFO, scaled by Age, makes the delay time drift. The mixer's limiter keeps the loop from running away.

Patch a sound into In L/R and take Out L/R onwards. Time is added to the delay time, Feedback to the feedback amount, Dark to the filter (positive makes it darker), Age to the drift and Mix to the dry/wet balance.

Tip: with Feedback high the loop self-oscillates into a murky drone; pull Dark back to keep it alive.

preset.description: Four low-pass gates side by side, each opened by its own LFO speed and spread across the stereo field, with a trigger input for each. Shared inputs Rate, Open, Tone, Ping 1 to 4 and Mix.

help.text:
The input goes to four Low Pass Gates. A Quad LFO in Divide mode runs them at rate ratios of 1, 1/2, 1/3 and 1/4, so their openings meet and part in a repeating pattern. Each gate has its own tone and pan, from dull and left to bright and right, and an Audio Mixer sums them.

Patch a sound into In L/R and take Out L/R onwards. Rate is added to the LFO speed, Open to how far all gates stay open, Tone to their brightness and Mix to the dry/wet balance. A trigger into Ping 1 to 4 plucks the matching gate on its own, which is the way to play it from a sequencer.

Tip: feed it a sustained pad; the four gates draw a slowly changing rhythm out of it.

preset.description: Ten frequency bands, each one's volume steered by how loud that band already is: push Sculpt up and the strong bands get stronger, pull it down and they even out. Shared inputs Sculpt, Tilt, Shift and Mix.

help.text:
A Filter Bank splits the sound into ten bands and reports the loudness of each. Every band goes to its own VCA, whose gain is a base level plus that band's loudness multiplied by Sculpt. With Sculpt positive the peaks of the spectrum are exaggerated; negative flattens them. Odd bands go to the left and even bands to the right, so the result is wide as well.

Patch a sound into In L/R and take Out L/R onwards. Sculpt is added to the sculpting amount, Tilt to the bank's tilt, Shift to how far the whole set of bands moves up or down in pitch, and Mix to the dry/wet balance.

Tip: modulate Shift with a slow LFO on a held chord for a moving, vowel-like colour.

preset.description: Four VCAs in one cell with a shared response control that bends their gain CV from straight to squared, a mix bus with spread and master, and a direct output for each channel. Shared inputs In 1 to 4, Gain 1 to 4, Response and Master.

help.text:
Each of the four inputs has its own VCA. Its gain is one by default plus the Gain CV for that channel, which makes the channel louder when you patch an envelope (up to twice) and leaves it alone when nothing is patched. A Multiplier squares the CV, and a Crossfader blends between the straight and the squared CV with Response, so the same envelope can move from a linear to a curved swell.

Patch audio into In 1 to 4. Out L/R is the mix bus (a four-channel mixer with its channels spread from left to right, and a limiter); Out 1 to 4 are the VCAs on their own, before the mixer. Response is added to the crossfade and Master to the mixer's master level.

Tip: one envelope into Gain 1 and Gain 2 and another into Gain 3 and Gain 4 makes a quick four-way cross-swell.

preset.description: A gentle tone curve: a clean low cut, more weight in the bottom, less boxiness at 300 Hz and a lift of air on top. Shared inputs Weight and Air.

help.text:
One EQ with four bands in use: a 24 dB/oct low cut at 28 Hz, a low shelf at 85 Hz (+2 dB), a wide dip at 300 Hz (-2.5 dB) and a high shelf at 10 kHz (+3 dB), plus a slight bell at 3 kHz for presence.

Patch a sound into In L/R and take Out L/R onwards. Weight is added to the gain of the low shelf and Air to the gain of the high shelf, so each moves the curve by up to about 9 dB at full amount.

Tip: put it last on a mix; turn Air up until the top opens, then back off a little.

preset.description: A slow, gentle compressor that listens only above 150 Hz, so the bass cannot make the mix pump: it holds drums, bass and chords together. Shared inputs Threshold and Mix.

help.text:
A Compressor in RMS mode with a low ratio, a slow 30 ms attack and a soft knee. Its Sidechain input gets a copy of the signal through a 1-pole high-pass at 150 Hz, so loud bass notes do not control the gain reduction. A light shelf on top adds a little polish afterwards.

Patch a sound into In L/R and take Out L/R onwards. Threshold is subtracted from the compressor's Threshold knob (more means more compression) and Mix is added to its Mix knob, which blends the squeezed sound with the dry one.

Tip: on a drum bus, set Threshold so the needle moves two to four decibels on loud hits.

preset.description: Tape-style saturation with a bit of supply sag, rounded off by a soft top cut and a little extra bottom: the warmth of a good machine. Shared inputs Drive and Tone.

help.text:
A Saturator in its Tape character with moderate drive, some sag, followed by an EQ with a low shelf at 100 Hz (+1.5 dB) and a gentle high cut at 14 kHz.

Patch a sound into In L/R and take Out L/R onwards. Drive is added to the Saturator's Drive knob and Tone to its Tone knob, which sets the top end of the saturated signal. It does not follow the transport.

Tip: it works on almost anything; try it on drums for glue or on a synth to soften digital edges.

preset.description: A tone curve, a medium compressor and a brickwall limiter in a row: it makes a mix louder and more even without falling over. Shared inputs Push and Bright.

help.text:
Three stages: an EQ (low cut at 30 Hz, a lift at 90 Hz, a dip at 350 Hz and a high shelf), a Compressor at 3:1 with a 15 ms attack, and a Limiter with a ceiling at -1 dB.

Patch a sound into In L/R and take Out L/R onwards. Push is added to the Limiter's Input knob (up to +24 dB at full amount, so a small turn is enough) and Bright to the high shelf's gain.

Tip: raise Push until the loudest parts just touch the limiter, and leave the rest of the headroom alone.

preset.description: The loudness of what you play opens a resonant band-pass: hard notes make it quack, soft notes keep it closed. Shared inputs Sensitivity and Cutoff.

help.text:
An Envelope Follower listens to the input and its output opens the cutoff of an SVF Band-pass filter with medium-high resonance. The follower reacts in a few milliseconds and falls back in a quarter of a second, which is the typical quack.

Patch a sound into In L/R and take Out L/R onwards. Sensitivity is added to the follower's Gain (how far the wah opens for a given loudness) and Cutoff to the filter's resting cutoff.

Tip: it loves funky guitar, clavinet and bass; play with a lot of dynamics and set Sensitivity so the loudest note just opens the filter fully.

preset.description: Two resonant band-passes side by side, the second pulled away from the first, slowly drifting: a sound seems to change vowels as it plays. Shared inputs Cutoff and Spread.

help.text:
A Dual Filter in Parallel routing with two band-pass sections and medium resonance. The second filter sits above the first by Spread. A slow LFO named Drift moves the shared cutoff, so the pair glides across vowel-like positions.

Patch a sound into In L/R and take Out L/R onwards. Cutoff is added to the shared cutoff and Spread to the distance between the two peaks. It does not follow the transport.

Tip: it needs a source with plenty of harmonics, like a saw, a pulse, strings or noise.

preset.description: Silences everything below a threshold so noise, hum and spill between notes disappear: the gate closes with a short, smoothed release. Shared inputs Threshold and Release.

help.text:
An Envelope Follower with a threshold turns the input into a gate signal, a Utility named Smooth slews it so the edges do not click, and a VCA applies it to the sound.

Patch a sound into In L/R and take Out L/R onwards. Threshold is added to the follower's threshold (higher means more is cut) and Release is added to its release, which also lengthens the time the gate stays open after a hit.

Tip: set Threshold just above the noise floor; on drums, shorten Release for a tight, punchy sound.

preset.description: A high-passed copy delayed by a different few milliseconds on each side is added under the dry sound: mono sources spread out without phasing the bass. Shared inputs Width and Time.

help.text:
The dry sound passes straight through. A copy goes through a 1-pole high-pass at 250 Hz, a Delay with 12 ms on the left and 23 ms on the right, and a VCA named Width into the output. Because the low end is left out of the copy, the bass stays centred and solid.

Patch a sound into In L/R and take Out L/R onwards. Width is added to the VCA gain and Time to both delay times. Check the result in mono; very high Width can thin out the sound.

Tip: use it on mono synths, guitars or vocals that sound narrow next to a stereo bed.

preset.description: A crushed and folded copy of the sound is blended with the clean one: drums and basses gain bite and weight without losing their shape. Shared inputs Grit and Blend.

help.text:
The sound goes down two paths: one stays clean, the other passes a Crunch (8 bits, reduced sample rate, tone at 6 kHz) and then a Folder. A Crossfader blends the two.

Patch a sound into In L/R and take Out L/R onwards. Grit is added to the Crunch Drive and the Folder's Fold, so one control makes the dirty path nastier; Blend is added to the Crossfader and sets how much of it you hear.

Tip: for a drum loop, keep Blend around a third and push Grit; for a bass, lower both.

preset.description: Harsh S sounds and hi-hat sizzle around 6 to 8 kHz pull the whole sound down for a moment and nothing else does: a vocal or a bright mix stays smooth. Shared inputs Amount and Frequency.

help.text:
A band-pass filter at 6.5 kHz listens to the input and feeds the Sidechain input of a fast Compressor. When the band is loud (an S or a hi-hat), the compressor turns the whole signal down for a few milliseconds; otherwise the sound passes untouched.

Patch a sound into In L/R and take Out L/R onwards. Amount is subtracted from the compressor's Threshold (higher means more de-essing) and Frequency is added to the listening filter's cutoff.

Tip: sweep Frequency while a vocal plays until the harshest S is tamed, then lower Amount until the effect is hardly audible.

preset.description: Six looping slopes locked to the bar whose speeds are spread over the overtone series (1, 2, 3, 4 ... times the bar), plus their sum: polyrhythmic movement for filters, pans and levels. Shared inputs Harmonics and Skew.

help.text:
A Six Slopes module in Loop mode, synced to one bar. Harmonics spreads the six rates over the overtone series, so slope 2 runs twice as fast as slope 1, slope 3 three times, and so on; all of them realign on the downbeat. Skew is the position of each slope's peak. Sum adds all six together.

There is no audio. Patch Slope 1 to 6 into any knobs, for example cutoffs of different filters, or Sum into one parameter for a complex rhythmic pulse. Harmonics is added to the Harmonics knob: pull it down to spread the rates over the undertones (slower and slower) instead. Skew is added to the Skew knob. It follows the transport.

Tip: send the slowest slopes to cutoff and the fastest to pan for movement at two timescales.

preset.description: One slow sine in four phases, 0, 90, 180 and 270 degrees apart: patch them into pans, cutoffs or detunes to make things orbit around each other. Shared inputs Rate and Reset.

help.text:
A Quad LFO in Quadrature mode. All four LFOs are sines running at the same rate, a quarter of a cycle apart, so when one is at its top the next is halfway between its top and bottom. The default rate is one cycle in about eight seconds.

There is no audio. Patch the four outputs into knobs: 0 and 180 into the pans of two oscillators for circular stereo movement, or 0 and 90 as X and Y of anything that wants a circle. The Rate input is added to the Rate knob, and a trigger into Reset restarts the cycle together on all four. It does not follow the transport.

Tip: put 0 on a filter cutoff and 90 on a resonance for a swirling, never-repeating sweep.

preset.description: Sidechain-style ducking without a sidechain: a rising swell restarts on every quarter note, scaled so the level dips and recovers like a pumping compressor. Patch Duck into a VCA's gain or a mixer. Shared input Depth.

help.text:
A Shape Env in Loop mode, synced to quarter notes, plays a logarithmic swell on every beat: it starts at zero and rises quickly. A Utility scales it so that it never goes lower than a floor of about 20 percent. At full height it is exactly one, so it can multiply a signal without changing its loudness.

There is no audio. Patch Duck into the Gain of a VCA after a pad, or into a mixer level, to make it pump with the beat. Beat is a trigger once per quarter note, and Ramp rises from 0 to 1 over each beat. The Depth input is added to the dip: more means a deeper duck, up to full silence on the beat. It follows the transport.

Tip: patch Duck into a pad and Ramp into a filter cutoff for a pumping that also opens the sound.

preset.description: Records any control movement while Record is held and replays it as a four-bar loop, in sync with the song, at any speed or backwards. Patch a Dial or XY Pad into In and a Button into Record.

help.text:
A Chart Recorder with a paper strip four bars long that follows the transport. While a gate is high on Record, the pen draws what is on In onto the strip; when it goes low, the strip keeps replaying what is on it as a loop, smoothly interpolated. Pen is the live value of the pen, Replay is the stored movement, and Marker is a trigger at the start of every pass.

There is no audio. Patch a Dial or an XY Pad into In, a Button into Record, and Replay into whatever you want to move. The Speed input is added to the replay speed: up speeds the loop up, and down slows it, stops it or plays it backwards. It follows the transport.

Tip: record a filter sweep during the first pass, then change other things by hand while it keeps going.

preset.description: Turns every trigger into a burst of four evenly spaced pulses: patch a clock or a drum trigger into Trigger and the Gate into an envelope for ratchets, flams and rolls. Shared inputs Trigger and Spacing.

help.text:
A Pulse Generator in Triggered mode with burst count four: each trigger starts a short train of four exact pulses, 50 milliseconds apart, each 15 milliseconds wide. Gate carries the pulses as gates; Sync is a trigger at the start of each pulse, which is better for drum voices that only need a trigger.

There is no audio. Patch a clock, a sequencer trigger or a button into Trigger, and Gate or Sync into an envelope or drum voice. The Spacing input is added to the pulse period: more means a slower roll, less a faster buzz that becomes a flam when it is short enough. It does not follow the tempo.

Tip: put the burst on snare hits only, and leave kicks and hats alone, for a drum roll that never gets muddy.

preset.description: Six gates that fire every 1, 2, 3, 5, 8 and 13 steps of a sixteenth-note clock, and a Rotate input that moves the whole set up the series: a lopsided but musical set of rhythms. Shared inputs Rotate and Reset.

help.text:
A Rotating Divider on the Fibonacci set, with a base of sixteenth notes, outputs gates every 1, 2, 3, 5, 8 and 13 steps. Because these numbers have no common rhythm, the combined result drifts through the bar and only all realigns after many bars; Align is a trigger when it does. Stair is a staircase signal that rises one step for every rotation.

There is no audio. Patch the six gates into drum voices, envelopes or sequencer clocks. The Rotate input is added to the Rotate knob, changing the divisions assigned to each output at the next bar: higher values give slower outputs. A trigger into Reset restarts all of them. It follows the transport unless you patch Clock.

Tip: put 1 and 2 on a hat, 3 on a clap, 5 on a kick and 8 and 13 on accents.

preset.description: Combines up to three gates with AND, OR and XOR, halves the first one with a flip-flop and gives a trigger for each change: new rhythms from rhythms you already have. Shared inputs Gate A, Gate B and Gate C.

help.text:
A Logic module with three gate inputs. And is high only when A, B and C are all high; Or when any is; Xor when an odd number of them are. Half is a flip-flop that changes state on every rising edge of A, so it is A divided by two. Change is a trigger on every rising or falling edge of the combined result.

There is no audio. Patch gates from drum voices, clocks or sequencers into the three inputs (an unpatched input is low), and the outputs into envelopes or drum voices. It does not have a clock of its own, so it follows whatever you patch in.

Tip: Xor of a kick and a hat pattern gives a rhythm that plays where only one of them does.

preset.description: Each trigger starts an eight-bar logarithmic ramp with three marker triggers on the way: automate a build-up by patching Sweep into a cutoff or a send. Shared inputs Trigger and Hold.

help.text:
A Sweep Generator in Triggered mode glides from its start to its stop frequency over eight bars, on a logarithmic law, so the first bars move fast and the last move slowly like a rising pitch. Sweep is the ramp from 0 to 1, Pitch is the sweeping frequency as pitch, and three Markers fire as it passes 250 Hz, 1 kHz and 4 kHz. End is a trigger at the top.

There is no audio. Patch a trigger or a Button into Trigger to start a build, Sweep into a filter cutoff, a reverb mix or a drum level, and Marker into a drum voice or a sequencer's Reset for fills along the way. A gate into Hold freezes the sweep where it is. It follows the transport.

Tip: Pitch into an oscillator makes a rising siren, matching the filter sweep.

preset.description: A small performance surface for the board: an XY pad, a big dial and a button, each smoothed so moves never click. Patch the outputs into any knobs, and play the pad from the cell's front panel.

help.text:
Three controllers in one cell: an XY Pad, a Dial and a Button. The pad and the dial are smoothed so that even fast moves do not click. The button gives a gate while it is held and a trigger when it is pressed.

There is no audio and no inputs. Patch X and Y into two parameters, such as a cutoff and a reverb mix, Macro into a third parameter such as a level, Hold into a gate input of an envelope, and Press into a trigger input. Everything is played by hand on the front panel of the cell, or by automating the knobs from the host.

Tip: use X and Y on two related parameters (cutoff and resonance) so one gesture moves both.

preset.description: Follows the loudness of any audio you patch into In and turns it into a smooth level, an inverted level and a gate and trigger when it is loud enough: let a drum loop move a filter or duck a pad. Shared inputs In and Threshold.

help.text:
An Envelope Follower with a fast attack and a medium release. Level rises with the loudness of the audio on In; Inverted is the mirror image, which is what you want for ducking: patch it into the Gain of a VCA after the signal you want to duck. Gate is high while the signal is above the threshold and Trigger fires each time it crosses upwards.

Patch audio into In (a drum bus, a bass, a vocal). It passes nothing on; it only listens. Threshold is added to the threshold knob of the gate: higher means that only louder hits count. The release time sets how smoothly the level falls. It does not need the transport.

Tip: kick drum in, Inverted on a pad's VCA gain: a real sidechain duck that follows the actual kick.

preset.description: Dense random drops on three bright noise-band voices of different pitch, panned across a small room: steady rain on a metal roof that never repeats. Shared input Intensity (drizzle to downpour).

help.text:
A Recall module on thirty-second notes makes random gates in Chance mode; a Coin Toss splits them between three Perc Voices in Noise Bank mode, each tuned to a different pitch and given a very short decay, so they sound like drops hitting sheet metal. The random voltages of Recall nudge each pitch, and a small reverb is the room.

Press play: it makes sound on its own from Out L/R. The Intensity input is added to the gate bias of Recall: lower is a drizzle, higher is a downpour. It follows the transport.

Tip: automate Intensity slowly up and down as a storm passing.

preset.description: The same twelve-step wooden pattern played by two clocks a hair apart: the two parts slowly slide out of phase and back again over minutes, a minimalist hand-clapping piece. Shared input Drift (widens the gap).

help.text:
Two LFO squares run freely at 6.00 and 6.03 steps per second. Each clocks its own Gate Sequencer with the same twelve-step pattern of eight hits, and each plays a Ring Rim Clave, one tuned a little higher and panned left, the other right. Because the second clock is slightly faster, it gains one step on the first about every 33 seconds; after twelve steps the two are in step again.

Press play: it plays on its own from Out L/R. The Drift input is added to the second clock's rate: a little makes the phasing faster. The clocks are free and do not follow the transport.

Tip: with Drift at zero, listen for the moment the parts line up again after about six and a half minutes.

preset.description: A gamelan-style cycle: a fast bar plays random notes, and slower bells and a deep gong strike on every 4th, 8th and 16th beat, so the layers meet only at the end of each long cycle. Shared input Rotate (moves the divisions).

help.text:
A Rotating Divider on the Powers of 2 set with a quarter-note base fires four layers at different divisions. The fastest strikes a bright bar tuned to random notes of D minor pentatonic, the next a mid bell, the next a low plate and the slowest a deep gong with a long ring. Together they mark the structure of the cycle: the gong closes it.

Press play: it plays on its own from Out L/R. The Rotate input is added to the Rotate knob and shifts the divisions at the next bar: more means slower layers. It follows the transport.

Tip: change the divider's Base to 1/8 for a faster, tighter cycle.

preset.description: A hazy dub-techno loop: soft kick, offbeat hats and a minor seventh chord stab fed into a long dotted echo and a cavernous reverb, so the chord dissolves into the fog. Shared inputs Cutoff and Dub (echo feedback).

help.text:
A Gate Sequencer plays a Ring Kick, closed hats, a ghost rim and the chord. The chord comes from a Chord Osc on a minor seventh, through a ladder filter and a short envelope. A dotted-eighth Delay Network with a lot of feedback and a big reverb sit on a send, so only the first hit is clear and the rest is fog.

Press play: it plays on its own from Out L/R. The Cutoff input is added to the chord filter cutoff, and Dub is added to the echo feedback: raise it for a wash, lower it to hear the pattern. It follows the transport.

Tip: ride Dub up on the last bar of a phrase, then back to zero on the downbeat.

preset.description: Rare random sine pings that sweep downward, one high and one deep, thrown into a dark, scattered echo and a huge reverb: a submarine listening in the deep. Shared input Activity (more pings).

help.text:
A Recall module on half notes makes sparse random gates in Chance mode. One starts a Sweep Generator that glides a sine from 2.4 kHz down to 700 Hz in under half a second; the other starts a second generator for a deep, slow ping from 280 Hz to 110 Hz. Both go into a dark Delay Network with scattered taps and a very long reverb.

Press play: it plays on its own from Out L/R. The Activity input is added to the gate bias of Recall: higher means more pings. It follows the transport.

Tip: it works well as a background under slow pads: set Activity so you hear a ping every few seconds.

preset.description: A dark drone of two fifths and a minor third whose level and filter beat like a slow heart, once a half note, under a bed of dark noise and a long reverb. Shared inputs Cutoff and Depth (shallow to deep beat).

help.text:
Three low oscillators (a root, a fifth and a minor third) and a little dark noise go through a ladder filter and a VCA. A looping Shape Env plays the Heartbeat shape once every half note: it opens the VCA and nudges the filter, so the drone swells with two quick pulses and sinks back. A slow organic LFO moves the cutoff and a long reverb sits around it.

Press play: it plays on its own from Out L/R. Cutoff is added to the filter cutoff, Depth is added to the heartbeat depth: at zero the drone still breathes a little, higher it pulses deeply. It follows the transport.

Tip: automate Depth up slowly as a scene tightens.

preset.description: Three pulse-formant voices on an A minor triad sing with vowels that drift independently and a faint wobble in the pitch, through chorus and a wide hall: a choir that never says the same word. Shared input Vowel.

help.text:
Three Formant Osc voices (A, E and A an octave apart) make a bright pulse with a moving resonant peak, which sounds like a sung vowel. Organic LFOs move each voice's formant independently and add a little pitch wobble, so the vowels shift from ah to oh to ee in no pattern. The sum goes through a chorus and a wide hall.

Press play: it plays on its own from Out L/R and is not tied to the tempo. The Vowel input is added to the formant of all three voices together: raise it to brighten the vowels, lower it to darken them.

Tip: automate Vowel with a slow LFO for a synchronised change of word across the choir.

preset.description: A sixteen-step G major lullaby on a bright struck bar with a low bell at the end of each round; Variation lets random steps wander, and a wobbly tape echo makes the whole box sound old. Shared input Variation.

help.text:
A Step Sequencer plays sixteen steps in G major on eighth notes. Each note strikes a bright Modal Voice tuned like a small wooden bar. At the end of each round a second voice, an octave lower, strikes a soft bell. A Zone Delay with tape wobble gives the sound an old, drifting character.

Press play: it plays on its own from Out L/R. The Variation input is added to the sequencer's Variation: at zero the lullaby is exactly the same every time, higher some steps jump by up to seven semitones, so the tune mutates round by round. It follows the transport.

Tip: set the starting Variation on the sequencer a little above zero and let it run for a while.

preset.description: Four related rhythms from a Rhythm Bank play a kick, snare, hat and rim in a warm saturated mix, and every four bars a slow random leafs to a new groove. Shared inputs Pattern and Drive.

help.text:
A Rhythm Bank in the Interlock family gives four rhythms that are related and avoid colliding with each other, each patched to a Ring drum voice: kick, snare, closed hat and rim. A slow Random module changes the pattern number every four bars, so the groove changes in steps, and the mix goes through a warm Saturator and a small room.

Press play: it plays on its own from Out L/R. The Pattern input is added to the pattern number: use it to choose a different set of grooves; Drive is added to the saturator drive for more crunch. It follows the transport.

Tip: set the Random module's Loop higher to make the changes come back in a repeating sequence of four.

preset.description: Three bowed glass-plate voices whose bows start and stop on their own loops of 17, 23 and 31 seconds, each choosing a fresh D major pentatonic note whenever it starts: slow, singing, always-new chords. Shared input Bow (pressure).

help.text:
Three Modal Voices in a plate-like geometry are bowed continuously while their gate is high. Each gate is a free LFO square with a loop length of 17, 23 or 31 seconds, so the bows overlap in changing ways. A Quantizer Suite fed by slowly fluctuating curves from an Uncertainty module samples a new D major pentatonic pitch each time a bow starts. The sum goes through a big reverb.

Press play: it plays on its own from Out L/R and is not tied to the tempo. The Bow input is added to the bow pressure of all three voices: more pressure is louder and rougher, less is breathy and soft.

Tip: reduce the bow pressure for a ghostly, whistling sound.

preset.description: Four slightly detuned oscillators on A and E under a low-pass that opens and closes over a minute, like a tide coming in and going out. Shared input Tide (speeds up the motion).

help.text:
Four Oscillators (a root, a slightly wider copy of it, a fifth and an octave) go into a Ladder Tanh filter. Organic LFOs at about one cycle every forty seconds move the cutoff and the detune of the wide copy, so the chord slowly brightens, darkens and beats against itself. A large hall sits behind it.

It sounds on its own from Out L/R when placed; it is not tied to the tempo. The Tide input is added to the rate of the Organic LFOs: raise it and the tide turns faster.

Tip: lower the filter's Resonance to zero for a plainer, softer bed; raise it for a vowel-like hum.

preset.description: Two additive drones on A and E whose odd and even partials swap places and drift slightly out of tune with each other, lit by an octave-up shimmer in a vast hall. Shared input Shimmer.

help.text:
Two Additive Osc modules play sixty-four-partial saws, A and E. Organic LFOs move Odd/Even from hollow clarinet-like to bright and back, and nudge Stretch so the partials slide a little apart and together again, like glass picking up overtones. The mixer sends a part of the sound through a Pitch Shifter an octave up into the hall, where it blooms as a shimmer.

It sounds on its own from Out L/R; it is not tied to the tempo. The Shimmer input is added to the level of the shimmer feedback: at zero it is a thin veil, higher it climbs in octaves.

Tip: set Stretch higher on the modules for a bell-like version.

preset.description: Two formant voices a fifth apart hold a vowel while a ghost of band-passed breath moves around them: a long wordless chant that slowly turns from one vowel to another. Shared input Vowel.

help.text:
Two Formant Osc voices (D and A, low) make a resonant, voice-like pulse whose peak is moved by Organic LFOs, so the vowel wanders. A Noise module through a band-pass Multi Filter that also wanders gives a faint breath. Chorus and a warm hall finish it.

It sounds on its own from Out L/R; it is not tied to the tempo. The Vowel input is added to the formant of both voices: raise it to make the vowel brighter.

Tip: turn Narrow up on the voices for a more nasal, reedy chant.

preset.description: A warm 55 Hz sine from a lamp-stabilised test oscillator with a faint mains buzz, a triangle sub and brown noise, pushed gently into tape: the sound of a large building at night. Shared input Warmth.

help.text:
A Test Oscillator on its slow range hums near 55 Hz and drifts a little, as a real lamp-stabilised oscillator does; its Mains setting adds a faint buzz. An Oscillator two octaves below A adds weight and Noise in brown adds air. A Multi Filter keeps the top end down and a Saturator in Tape mode glues it together. A slow Organic LFO breathes the filter and the drive.

It sounds on its own from Out L/R; it is not tied to the tempo. The Warmth input is added to the saturator drive. This one is mostly low: check it on speakers that reproduce bass.

Tip: set Mains to Off on the Test Oscillator for a cleaner, purer tone.

preset.description: A cloud of twelve oscillators that gathers into a D minor ninth, then loosens back towards unison, never the same twice: a drone that breathes in chords. Shared input Bloom.

help.text:
A Swarm module plays twelve oscillators over a minor ninth chord. Spread is moved by an Organic LFO: at the low end they sit close to one note, at the high end they open into the whole chord and spread over the stereo field. Drift and Detune keep each one moving. A low-pass Multi Filter that opens a little with the bloom and a hall finish the sound.

It sounds on its own from Out L/R; it is not tied to the tempo. The Bloom input is added to Spread: it opens the chord.

Tip: Chord is a choice on the Swarm: try Fifths for a bare, open cloud, or Quartal for a suspended one.

preset.description: A minor add-nine chord from one Chord Osc smears into a long, wobbling tape echo that feeds on itself, so the chord blurs into a slowly turning cloud. Shared input Smear (echo feedback).

help.text:
A Chord Osc plays a C minor add-nine on five oscillators with some detune and stereo spread. A dark Multi Filter and a Saturator in Tape mode soften it, then a Zone Delay on its long zone with a lot of feedback and wobble repeats it into itself. A slow Organic LFO moves the filter.

It sounds on its own from Out L/R; it is not tied to the tempo. The Smear input is added to the echo feedback: higher builds a thicker cloud that can swell by itself, lower lets the chord stand.

Tip: Time on the Zone Delay changes the speed of the smear; because it is a tape delay, moving it bends the pitch.

preset.description: Two low oscillators rubbing against each other in slow FM, with a rumble of noise and a swell that rises and falls over half a minute: engines in the next valley. Shared input Rumble.

help.text:
A Dual Osc with both cores three octaves down, B tuned a fifth below A and a little FM from B into A, drifting at 60 %, so the two never agree. Brown Noise adds a rumble. A Tidal module in Loop mode moves the sound's level through a long swell, and the ladder filter after it opens and closes with an Organic LFO. A little hall at the end.

It sounds on its own from Out L/R; it is not tied to the tempo. The Rumble input is added to the FM depth: raise it for rougher engines.

Tip: Fold on the Dual Osc turns the engines into something much more metallic.

preset.description: Two wavetable oscillators on A and E gliding through the Vowel table in slow, unrelated paths, wrapped in chorus and an octave-up shimmer: coloured curtains of sound that fold over each other. Shared input Colour.

help.text:
Two Wavetable Osc modules read the Vowel bank. Organic LFOs move X and Y of each, so the table is scanned along paths that never repeat. A Chorus widens them and a Pitch Shifter an octave up sits in the hall's feedback path as a shimmer.

It sounds on its own from Out L/R; it is not tied to the tempo. The Colour input is added to Y of both oscillators: it moves the whole sound to a different row of the table.

Tip: change Bank to Spectra or Bell for a different family of veils.

preset.description: Three bowed bell bodies tuned to D, A and E that never stop singing, their bows swelling and relaxing on three slow cycles so the beating between them is always changing. Shared input Bow (pressure).

help.text:
