Three Modal Voices in a bell geometry are bowed without a break: a Utility that is always one acts as their gate. Organic LFOs vary each bow's pressure slowly and out of step, so one voice swells while another fades, and the three beat against each other. A large hall carries it.

It sounds on its own from Out L/R; it is not tied to the tempo. The Bow input is added to the pressure of all three: more is louder and rougher, less turns into thin whistling.

Tip: lower Damping on the voices for a longer shimmer after the bow dips.

preset.description: A rich harmonic oscillator on a low A passes through a frequency shifter that spirals back into itself, so slow swirls of overtones climb and sink around a steady fundamental. Shared input Spiral.

help.text:
A Macro Osc on its Harmonic model plays a low A. Organic LFOs move its Tone, Shape and Blend knobs slowly. A Freq Shifter on the plus or minus ten hertz range shifts it up by about one and a half hertz and feeds a part of itself back, which gives barber-pole phasing: the overtones seem to rise forever. A hall completes the sea.

It sounds on its own from Out L/R; it is not tied to the tempo. The Spiral input is added to the shifter feedback: more makes bells and swirls, too much turns into a roar.

Tip: set Shift to a negative amount for a spiral that sinks instead of rising.

preset.description: A stream of pink noise excites a resonant body of four voices that slowly changes structure: a thin, glassy ring like wind across the ice. Shared input Thaw (damping).

help.text:
A Noise module in pink goes into a Resonator in Modal mode with four voices. The constant noise keeps the modes ringing, so you hear their pitches as a soft tone cluster. Organic LFOs move Structure (from string-like to plate-like), Brightness and the tuning by a few semitones. A hall around it makes the lake.

It sounds on its own from Out L/R; it is not tied to the tempo. The Thaw input is added to Damping: higher makes the ring shorter and warmer, lower makes it glassier and thinner.

Tip: Frequency sets the pitch of the whole cluster; lower it by twelve for a bigger, darker lake.

preset.description: A soft major-seventh chord is recorded into a granular cloud that plays it back in large, overlapping grains drifting in position and pitch, with feedback so the cloud thickens and thins. Shared input Density.

help.text:
A Chord Osc plays a major seventh through a gentle filter into a Grains module. Organic LFOs move the read position, the grain size and the pitch scatter, while Feedback and Blur let the grains pile into a cloud. The result goes through a hall.

It sounds on its own from Out L/R; it is not tied to the tempo. The Density input is added to the density of the grains: at the low end a few separate swells, at the high end a solid fog.

Tip: Pitch Quant on the Grains module sets what the scatter is rounded to: Octaves + fifths keeps it consonant.

preset.description: Noise through a pair of resonant band-passes, one per ear, that wander on slow random curves while the whole wind swells and sinks over about half a minute: weather on a high, empty moor. Shared input Gust.

help.text:
A Noise module goes into a Dual Filter in Stereo routing, so each ear has its own resonant band-pass. An Uncertainty module's two fluctuating curves move the Cutoff and the Spread of the filters, so the whistling moves around. A Tidal module in Loop mode opens and closes a VCA over about thirty seconds, which is the breathing. A little room finishes it.

It sounds on its own from Out L/R; it is not tied to the tempo. The Gust input is added to the Cutoff: it makes the wind higher and more whistling.

Tip: turn the resonances (Res 1 and Res 2) up for a thin howl, or down for a soft rush.

preset.description: Rare random gates open long, slow swells on dark brown noise that grumble and roll away into a big room: thunder somewhere beyond the hills. Shared input Storm (more rolls).

help.text:
A Recall module in Chance mode, running free on its own clock, throws a rare gate. It opens an ADSR with a long attack and release, which swells a VCA on brown Noise through a low-pass whose cutoff rises with the swell. A second, slower voice with a lower filter rolls underneath. A large hall carries the rumble away.

It sounds on its own from Out L/R; it is not tied to the tempo. The Storm input is added to the gate bias of Recall: higher means more thunder.

Tip: put it under a rain cell, such as Tin Roof Rain, for a storm.

preset.description: Two sine voices a fifth apart that slide up and down on slow random curves and fade in and out of the dark, repeating into a long echo: calls across a very large ocean. Shared input Depth (echo).

help.text:
Two Oscillators in sine shape are bent in pitch by the smooth and wobble outputs of a Wobble module (a random stream), by up to seven semitones, so they glide in long calls. An Uncertainty module's curves fade each voice in and out through a VCA. A Delay Network with a lot of feedback and a dark tone repeats the calls, then a vast hall.

It sounds on its own from Out L/R; it is not tied to the tempo. The Depth input is added to the delay feedback: higher builds a chorus of echoes.

Tip: slow Wobble's Rate for fewer, longer calls.

preset.description: White noise through ten narrow bands tuned to the harmonic series of A, with a scanning window drifting up and down the spectrum: breathy overtones appear and vanish as if singing. Shared input Scan.

help.text:
A Noise module goes into a Filter Bank with Tuning on Harmonic: ten very narrow band-passes tuned to the first ten harmonics of A. An Organic LFO moves Scan, which chooses where along the spectrum the bands are loud, and another moves Tilt and Odd/Even, so the overtones come and go. Chorus and a hall widen it.

It sounds on its own from Out L/R; it is not tied to the tempo. The Scan input is added to the Scan knob: turn it by hand or automate it to play the overtones.

Tip: raise Q for a purer, more tonal result; lower it for a breathy rush.

preset.description: Soft swells of pink noise are caught in a long, worn tape loop that holds on to them and slowly turns them into something that sounds like a memory of rain. Shared input Memory (loop feedback).

help.text:
A Recall module in Chance mode makes a rare random gate. It opens a slow ADSR on pink Noise, a short swell. The swell goes through a Saturator in Tape mode with a lot of Age, then into a Zone Delay on its long zone with a lot of feedback and wobble: it loops, each pass duller and wobblier than the one before, until the next swell covers it.

It sounds on its own from Out L/R; it is not tied to the tempo. The Memory input is added to the feedback of the loop: at the top the loop never forgets.

Tip: raise Recall's T Bias on the module to feed the loop more often.

preset.description: Two radio-frequency carriers beating against each other make a low, wavering hum that a frequency shifter and a slow phaser pull into slowly turning, vaguely electrical weather. Shared input Pull.

help.text:
A Beat Oscillator mixes two high carriers and plays their difference as a low tone, wavering because Drift is high. Pull makes the two carriers want to lock together, so the tone sometimes stutters and settles. A Freq Shifter spirals it with a little feedback and a six-stage Phaser sweeps it slowly. A hall around it.

It sounds on its own from Out L/R; it is not tied to the tempo. The Pull input is added to Pull: higher stutters and locks more.

Tip: Beat sets the pitch of the difference tone; it moves in one big hum range, from 20 to 200 hertz.

preset.description: A set of sympathetic strings in D minor pentatonic that are brushed by rare random touches, so soft overtone clouds appear, ring together and fade into a big room. Shared input Touch (more strums).

help.text:
A Recall module in Chance mode running free makes rare gates and random voltages. A Quantizer holds the voltages to D minor pentatonic and sets the pitch of a Resonator in Sympathetic mode with four voices. Each gate strums it, and the strings ring together for a long time. An Organic LFO moves Brightness and Damping. A hall adds the room.

It sounds on its own from Out L/R; it is not tied to the tempo. The Touch input is added to the gate bias of Recall: more is more strums, up to a continuous shimmer.

Tip: switch the Resonator's Model to String for a more plucked version.

preset.description: A very narrow band-pass slowly sweeps up and down through white noise, lifting out single glassy whistles one after another and trailing them into a cold echo. Shared input Chill (echo feedback).

help.text:
A Wave Analyzer in Sweep mode runs a ten-hertz-wide band-pass across the whole spectrum over about a minute, up and then down, over a white Noise source. What comes out is a thin, pure whistle that glides. A Delay Network with scattered taps repeats it and a hall makes it cold and large.

It sounds on its own from Out L/R; it is not tied to the tempo. The Chill input is added to the delay feedback: higher leaves trails of old whistles.

Tip: set Range on the Wave Analyzer to 2 to 20 kHz for a high, thin version, or 20 to 200 Hz for deep rumbling pitches.

preset.description: Soft sine notes from D major pentatonic arrive at random, a few seconds apart, each opening a slow low pass gate and trailing off into a dark echo: a melody that never repeats itself. Shared input Chance (more notes).

help.text:
A Recall module running free makes random gates and random voltages every few seconds. A Quantizer holds the voltage to D major pentatonic and sets the pitch of a sine Oscillator. Each gate pings a Low Pass Gate in its slow-memory mode and starts an ADSR that opens it, which swells the note and lets it dim away. A Delay Network and a hall behind it make the notes ring on.

It sounds on its own from Out L/R; it is not tied to the tempo. The Chance input is added to the gate bias of Recall: higher means notes more often.

Tip: change Recall's Rate to set the pace of the whole piece; its Seed gives you a different melody.

preset.description: Two big bells in D Lydian struck at random by their own gates, a low one rarely and a high one a little more often, so they ring over each other for many seconds in a hall. Shared input Wind (more strikes).

help.text:
A Recall module running free makes two streams of random gates and random voltages. Each gate strikes a Modal Voice in a bell geometry with long ringing, one an octave below the other; each voltage goes through a Quantizer (D Lydian) to its pitch. The strikes land at random times, so the two bells ring into each other. A huge hall carries them.

It sounds on its own from Out L/R; it is not tied to the tempo. The Wind input is added to the gate bias of Recall: higher means more strikes.

Tip: Damping on the voices sets how long they ring: lower is longer.

preset.description: Three voices on slow glides that each pick a new note of A natural minor every eight seconds or so, singing a vowel that wanders: a choir at the end of the day that never quite resolves. Shared input Vowel.

help.text:
A Recall module running free makes three random voltages, one for each voice, a new set every few seconds. Three Quantizers (A natural minor) round them to notes with a long glide, and three Formant Osc voices sing them, an octave apart. Organic LFOs move each voice's formant so the vowel wanders. Chorus and a hall finish the choir.

It sounds on its own from Out L/R; it is not tied to the tempo. The Vowel input is added to the formant of all three voices.

Tip: Glide on each Quantizer decides how long a change takes; at zero the voices jump.

preset.description: Single plucked notes in E minor pentatonic, falling one by one into a long echo and a deep hall: a lone instrument in an empty hall at night. Shared input Touch (more plucks).

help.text:
A Recall module running free makes random gates and random voltages. A gate plucks a Macro Osc in its Pluck model; the voltage goes through a Quantizer (E minor pentatonic) to the pitch, A Delay Network with a lot of feedback and a dark tone repeats each note, and a hall holds the echoes.

It sounds on its own from Out L/R; it is not tied to the tempo. The Touch input is added to the gate bias of Recall: more is more plucks.

Tip: Decay on the Macro Osc sets how long a string rings; Tone and Shape change the instrument.

preset.description: A single chord oscillator carried from chord to chord of D Dorian by a slow random walk with long glides, so seventh chords melt into one another every ten seconds or so. Shared input Colour (brightness).

help.text:
A Random module makes a new voltage every ten seconds or so; a Quantizer (D Dorian, with a long glide) turns it into the pitch that drives a Chord Osc in Scale mode, so every chord is built from the notes of the scale: a different seventh chord each time, with the notes sliding into place. A low-pass Multi Filter opens and closes with an Organic LFO, then a chorus and a large hall.

It sounds on its own from Out L/R; it is not tied to the tempo. The Colour input is added to the filter cutoff.

Tip: Chord on the Chord Osc chooses the kind of chords; Sus2 or Sus4 give a more open sound.

preset.description: Two leaky neurons that excite and inhibit each other fire in an irregular rhythm that is never the same, striking two soft wooden bars in G major pentatonic, like a lullaby played by a sleepy machine. Shared input Excite.

help.text:
A Neuron module with a steady bias fires two neurons whose spikes feed each other, so the rhythm is irregular but has a character. Each spike strikes a Modal Voice tuned like a soft wooden bar; the pitches come from a Wobble module's stepped random stream, held by a Quantizer to G major pentatonic. A Zone Delay on tape gives each note a soft echo and a hall sits behind.

It sounds on its own from Out L/R; it is not tied to the tempo. The Excite input is added to the bias of the first neuron: higher fires faster.

Tip: Leak on each neuron sets how fast it forgets; change it to change the rhythm's feel.

preset.description: Soft kalimba-like notes in A major pentatonic whose density rises and falls in a slow tide: sometimes one note every few seconds, sometimes a shimmering handful, always in a tape echo. Shared input Tide.

help.text:
A Recall module running free makes random gates and voltages at a quick pace; an Organic LFO moves the gate bias in a slow tide, so the notes come in clusters and then die away. The voltages go through a Quantizer (A major pentatonic) to the pitch of a Modal Voice tuned like a small tine, and a tape echo and a hall hold the notes.

It sounds on its own from Out L/R; it is not tied to the tempo. The Tide input is added to the gate bias: lifts the whole level of activity.

Tip: Rate on Recall sets the fastest note rate a cluster can reach.

preset.description: Two bowed string bodies that swell in and out on loops of 21 and 29 seconds, each picking a new note of E harmonic minor as it starts: a slow, plaintive duet that is never twice the same. Shared input Bow (pressure).

help.text:
Two Modal Voices in a string geometry are bowed while their gate is high. Each gate is a free LFO square at a loop length of 21 or 29 seconds, so the two swell in and out in changing combinations. A Wobble module's stepped stream, held by a Quantizer in E harmonic minor, supplies each voice with a note, sampled when the bow starts. A hall holds the tone.

It sounds on its own from Out L/R; it is not tied to the tempo. The Bow input is added to the pressure of both voices.

Tip: Contour sets how slowly the bow swells in; raise it for a gentler start.

preset.description: A Swarm of fifths on a slow random walk through C major pentatonic that reshuffles its voices every minute or so, so the choir keeps finding a new arrangement of the same few notes. Shared input Light (brightness).

help.text:
A Random module walks very slowly through voltages that a Quantizer rounds to C major pentatonic, with a long glide, as the pitch of a Swarm in Fifths mode with ten oscillators. An LFO's cycle pulse, once a minute or so, reshuffles which oscillator plays which note. A low-pass Multi Filter opens with an Organic LFO, then chorus and a hall.

It sounds on its own from Out L/R; it is not tied to the tempo. The Light input is added to the filter cutoff.

Tip: Pattern on the Swarm changes how the notes are laid across the stereo field.

preset.description: High, glassy tones with stretched overtones appear at random in D Lydian, each one blooming and dying over several seconds into a big hall: wet fingers on the rims of wine glasses. Shared input Touch (more tones).

help.text:
A Recall module running free makes random gates and voltages. Each gate triggers an Additive Osc with a stretched, bell-like spectrum and a long decay; each voltage goes through a Quantizer (D Lydian) to its pitch. The tones are sent to a Pitch Shifter an octave up as well and to a very large hall.

It sounds on its own from Out L/R; it is not tied to the tempo. The Touch input is added to the gate bias of Recall: more is more tones.

Tip: Stretch on the Additive Osc changes the metal: lower is more string, higher more bell.

preset.description: A blank Voice Cell: notes in, nothing inside yet. Open the board and patch your own voice between Voice In and Voice Out.

help.text:
A Voice Cell with nothing inside except a cable that keeps the voice alive while a key is held, so it is silent.

Open the cell, add your modules, and cable Voice In (pitch, gate, trigger, velocity) into them and into Voice Out. Patch Notes in and take Out L/R.

Tip: an Oscillator from the pitch jack, into a VCA opened by an ADSR, is the smallest voice.

preset.description: A blank effect: the audio passes straight through. Open the board and put your own modules between In and Out.

help.text:
A stereo effect cell with nothing inside: In L/R are cabled straight to Out L/R, so audio passes unchanged.

Patch audio into In L/R and take Out L/R. Open the cell and put your own modules between In and Out.

Tip: remove the straight pass-through cables once your own chain is cabled in.

preset.description: A pentatonic melody that plays with the transport, through Verb (medium room). Move Size, Decay and Mix while it plays; Mix at 100 % leaves only the tail.

help.text:
A Step Sequencer plays a C major pentatonic melody with the transport, through an Oscillator and the Verb module. It has no inputs; take Out L/R.

Press play in the host and the melody starts. Open the cell to change the Verb's Size, Decay and Mix.

Tip: set Mix to 100 % to hear only the tail.
